speaker: Ulisses Soares
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: A Higher and Holier Fast
summary: Elder Soares teaches that the law of the fast, joined with earnest prayer and generous fast offerings, is an act of worship that draws us near to God and turns our hearts to His children. He builds the talk on Isaiah 58 and its promise that our light will break forth as the morning and the Lord will say "Here I am," with the Savior's 40-day fast in the wilderness as the pattern. He invites members to ponder Isaiah and live the fast in a higher and holier way, promising miracles, strength over weakness and greater sensitivity to others.

See counsel, including for those who are not able to fast, from President Russell M. Nelson: “For all whose health may permit, let us fast, pray, and unite our faith once again. … How do we fast? Two meals or a period of 24 hours is customary. But you decide what would constitute a sacrifice for you, as you remember the supreme sacrifice the Savior made for you” (“Opening the Heavens for Help,” Liahona, May 2020, 74). See also this counsel from President Joseph F. Smith: “Many are subject to weakness, others are delicate in health, and others have nursing babies; of such it should not be required to fast. Neither should parents compel their little children to fast” (Gospel Doctrine, 5th ed. [1939], 244). See also General Handbook: Serving in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, 38.8.17.
